title: On the complexity of the single-move labeled token routing problem
summary: In neutral-atom quantum computers, atoms are moved to target positions along paths of empty positions, and a target position may be reserved for one species of atom. Motivated by this task, we introduce Single-Move Labeled Token Routing: every source and every target vertex of a graph is assigned a set of labels, and tokens occupy the sources. A solution consists of a matching that assigns each source to a compatible target (one whose label set intersects its own), a route for each matched pair, and a movement order in which, when a token is moved, its route contains no other token.
